utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Would the witness kindly take the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Please make yourself comfortable. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, please state your full name.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: My name is Nenad Krejic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: As we discussed the other day, part of your evidence is -- in this case is going to be submitted in writing, and we need to first deal with the formalities associated with that submission. You provided a statement to representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY, and you've also testified as a witness in the BH state court and also before this Tribunal in the Stanisic and Zupljanin trial on the 1st and 2nd of September, 2010. You've subsequently had an opportunity to review the audio recordings of your testimony in the Stanisic and Zupljanin case and you wish to provide a number of clarifications. These clarifications were read back to you and you agreed with them, and I think the simplest way for me to do it is go through the clarifications as you indicated and then if you can simply affirm with a yes or a no whether I have stated the clarification you wish to make correctly. So the first clarification is in relation to English transcript page 14046, and this is in 65 ter number 0 -- 90287, and it's starting at line 13, and you wished to clarify that your answer where you said: "In our municipality --" I'll start again, quote: "In our municipality there had been no war crimes, no mass or multiple murders, and the public saw this incident as something that is going to besmirch our municipality." And the clarification that you wanted to make is that it doesn't imply that the massacre at Koricanske Stijene occurred in the territory of the Skender Vakuf municipality which was subsequently renamed the Knezevo municipality; that is correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: I am not sure that I understood the last bit of your question properly. When you were talking about Koricanske Stijene and its location, although during proofing we did clarify that. Could you please repeat that bit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Basically the correction you wanted to make to the transcript page at 14 -- it wasn't a correction, it was a clarification, at transcript page 14046, was just the fact that when you referred in your answer to "there had been no war crimes, no mass or multiple murders," and the public saw this incident as something that was going to look badly upon your municipality, what you -- what you want to clarify is that this incident at Koricanske Stijene, at the actual site, occurred -- didn't occur on the territory of the Knezevo municipality, what was formally known as the Skender Vakuf municipality. And, in fact, you pointed that out in subsequent transcript pages, and that's at transcript page 14093, starting at line 25. You made reference to this fact that the site where the incident took place was in fact not on Knezevo municipality territory, and you also pointed it out again at transcript page 14100, starting at line 22. And that was the clarification that you wanted to -- to make, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Now I understood you, and I can answer that that was indeed the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the next clarification that you wanted to make is at transcript page 14030 starting at line 10, and you wished to clarify that in addition to the city of Knezevo - and this is when you were questioned, you were looking at the map, the ethnic breakdown map - and you wanted to clarify that in addition to the city of Knezevo, Muslims also lived in two small suburbs of the city of Knezevo called Sapani and Bastina, and both those suburbs are approximately 1 kilometre from the town of Knezevo, and they have approximately 30 houses in each. And additionally, at line 13 on the same transcript page, you wanted to clarify that there is actually a Croatian village of Pavlovici, but it is located in the Croat part of the municipality in the south-west area and not in the Serb part of the municipality in the north-west area, because you were taken to the map and you said that there is no village called Pavlici -- Pavlovici in the north-east area, and you're actually clarifying that, in fact, there is one there in the north-east area but there's also one in the south-west area which is where the Croat -- the Croat population lived; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The next clarification you wished to make was at transcript page 14035 starting at line 9, and in there you wished to clarify your answer, "The last convoy to leave Prijedor," by stating that it's actually the second-to-last convoy that arrived from Prijedor. Is that the clarification you wished to make to that transcript page?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: We had problems during proofing with regard to this particular answer, because you and I together established that in the transcript, it was erroneously interpreted. We listened to the audiotapes subsequently. I didn't say at the time that the convoy left from Prijedor as it was transcribed. I said that that convoy came from Prijedor. I did not want to particularly clarify this, so we established that last year during my testimony in the Zupljanin/Stanisic case I said, and that was confirmed by listening to the audiotape that, that convoy came from Prijedor. I never knew that it was misrecorded. However, in my clarification I only clarified that that was the penultimate convoy that came from Prijedor for as much as I knew and not the last one.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification, Mr. Krejic. The next clarification is in relation to transcript page 14125 starting at line 21, and that was when there was discussion about the Law on Internal Affairs, and at one point your answer at line 21, instead of beginning with the word "Yes," it should have started with "I don't remember that specific provision," but the remainder of the answer is correct that you give in the transcript. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The next clarification you want to make is at transcript page 14127 starting at line 16, and the clarification is that there the answer which begins your answer "Yes," it appears from -- from that that you're agreeing that the road was blocked throughout the war, which was put to you as part of the question, and you wish to clarify that the "Yes" referred to part of the question related to a Croat and not to the part of the question about the road being blocked, and you wanted to stress that the road was not blocked throughout the war. Is that correct, the clarification as I've just stated it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And finally a clarification on transcript page 14129, starting at line 11. You wish to clarify that the answer "Yes" at that point is not entirely accurate but that you clarified it in your further response after the break that was immediately taken, and that's at transcript page 14130, line 1. Is that the -- the clarification you wish to make?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Krejic, with those clarifications, do you agree that the transcript accurately reflects what you said at the time you gave evidence?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If you were asked today about the matters you testified to in the Stanisic and Zupljanin case with the clarifications that we've just gone through, would you provide the same information to the Chamber, and that is even if you couldn't formulate everything in the same words, the essence would be the same?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender 65 ter number 90287, which is the witness's Stanisic/Zupljanin testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P3760, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And with Your Honours' leave I'll read a summary of the witness's written evidence. Mr. Krejic is a Bosnian Serb from the Skender Vakuf municipality which was renamed Knezevo. During the relevant time period the witness was the chief of the Skender Vakuf/Knezevo SJB. The witness testified about the aftermath of the mass killing at Koricanske Stijene on the 21st of August, 1992. This is scheduled incident B, 15.6. The witness testified that he visited the site shortly after the massacre and saw between 150 and 200 bodies. He was told by policemen that members of the SJB Prijedor had admitted that they had killed the people at Koricanske Stijene. The witness was also told by men from his police unit that the perpetrators had robbed the persons on the convoy of money and gold. Further, the witness testified that immediately after viewing the site of the massacre, he reported his findings to Stojan Zupljanin, his superior, who was chief of the Banja Luka CSB. Shortly thereafter, the witness travelled to Banja Luka with Milan Komljenovic and Vladimir Glamocic who was the president of the Executive Board -- sorry, president of the municipality of Skender Vakuf, and Vladimir Glamocic who was President of the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly for a meeting with Stojan Zupljanin. Also present at the meeting were Milomir Stakic and Simo Drljaca from Prijedor, the president of the Municipal Assembly and the chief of police respectively. There were also others in this meeting, and you discussed the removal of the bodies of the massacre. The witness testified that people from Prijedor were present at the meeting -- sorry. I'll start again. The witness testified that people from Prijedor who were present at the meeting admitted that killings at Koricanske Stijene had been committed by policemen from Prijedor. The witness testified that at the meeting, Stojan Zupljanin read a dispatch sent by Radovan Karadzic ordering the municipal leaders from Prijedor and Skender Vakuf/Knezevo to deal with the matter. The witness testified that four or five days after the incident, members of the 22nd Brigade of the Army of Republika Srpska, the VRS, brought into the Skender Vakuf/Knezevo SJB a survivor of the massacre at Koricanske Stijene. Pursuant to an order from Zupljanin, the witness personally transported a survivor of the massacre to Banja Luka security service centre. In addition, the witness testified that he also attended a meeting in Banja Luka on the 30th of August, 1992. That meeting was chaired by Republika Srpska Minister of Defence Bogdan Subotic and attended by RS MUP and civilian authorities from Banja Luka, Prijedor, and Skender Vakuf/Knezevo where the recovery of the bodies from the massacre was discussed. The witness testified that after the meeting, Bogdan Subotic and other persons present at the meeting travelled to the site of the massacre. The witness testified that at the second visit of the site, he saw that the site of the massacre was not secured and that the civilian protection from Skender Vakuf/Knezevo had cut down shrubbery and underbrush to cover the bodies. The witness identified police officers involved in the recovery of the bodies when he was shown a video-tape. Your Honours, that concludes the summary of the witness's evidence. Mr. Krejic, I have no additional questions for you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we deal with associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In relation to the transcript, if I may, which is now Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes. There are a number of procedural matters which are dealt with within Mr. Krejic's testimony, and I was going to ensure that those transcript pages were redacted from the -- those procedural matters were redacted from the transcript that will form part of the exhibit, and if Your Honour wishes me to do read the transcript page references and where those procedural matters unrelated to the witness's evidence are dealt with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If the Defence does not object to, you can relay with the court deputy later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. And I seek to have admitted all the associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In relation to 65 ter 5554, list of members of Special Police detachment, can you upload it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'll make sure that that's done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, shall we upload it now so that we can see the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While it is being uploaded, 65 ter number 23497 and 23498, and as well as 23499, I take there's no objection from the Defence to add these documents to the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have the document on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I wanted to check and make sure that while the English page -- English version is of 20 pages, the B/C/S version is only 7 pages. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm -- I don't have the document, I'm sorry, in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's why I wanted to upload it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can go to the last page of the B/C/S. And the last page of the English. Your Honour, I'm sorry, there does appear to be an anomaly in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the witness referred to only two pages out of these 20 pages, so if you'd like to deal with this, I'd like to -- I'm sorry. I correct. If you'd like to tender this, I would like you to deal with this document with the witness now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, do you -- do you recognise this document that was shown to you in -- in your Stanisic/Zupljanin testimony?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go back to page 1, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you -- do you recognise this document as the document that was shown to you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: With the Trial Chamber's leave, I would like to say a few words about the summary that the Prosecutor has just read out and then I will answer the question. With your leave, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: By all means, Mr. Krejic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if this has been misinterpreted or something. I'm not a Bosnian Serb. I don't know if there are such Serbs at all. I'm a Serb by ethnicity, and I hail from the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I am a Serb. I was born in Bosnia-Herzegovina. I am not a Bosnian Serb. And another very important thing, I have a lot of objections, but there is a key objection that I would like to refer to, and that is that on two occasions it was mentioned at those meetings that were held in Banja Luka we spoke about the removal of the bodies. One can get an erroneous impression that there were two meetings where I participated actively and that the only subject of those two meetings was to eliminate the bodies from the crime site at Koricanske Stijene, which cannot be correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I can follow up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I can follow up with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Krejic, by the word -- when I used the word "removal," which was contained in the Stanisic/Zupljanin testimony, do you mean to recover the bodies for -- to be used so that -- for forensic examination and other things on it done to the bodies, for example, burials?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: At those meetings we discussed a number of things. Firstly, we established that a crime had been committed, that there were bodies there, and we discussed the launching of investigation and procedure, not just the removal, as you simply put it. And then when you said "removal," in the same breath you said to move the bodies and to bury them, but there were other things mentioned as well. For example, that those bodies should be moved, that they should be taken out from the -- from that gorge and buried. There were discussions about launching investigation and prosecuting all those who were responsible for -- for the crime.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Krejic, can you look at the document that's on the screen, which is the document that was shown to you during your Stanisic/Zupljanin testimony. We can see that it's a list of the members of the Banja Luka CSB Special Police detachment and it's the payroll for August 1992. It lists 167 names there. Were you aware of this Special Police detachment attached to CSB Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And looking -- looking at the names there on the first page, are any of those -- you said that you -- no, I'm sorry. I withdraw that question. Are you aware of these people being in the special detachment? The names that you see on this first page.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: I know only some of these people, not all.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the people that you know, can you say the number next to their name?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I know some people by sight, but I don't know that the person's name is, for instance, Mirko Lukic, although I happen to know the man. I'll only tell you the names of those people where I can match the face with the name. Number 2, Ljuban Ecim; then 3, Zdravko Samardzija; number 4, Nenad Kajkut; number 7, Trifko Buha; number 10, Danko Kajkut; 12, Stevo Karakas. Number 15 and 18, two last names -- in fact, the same last name, Prastalo, I don't know which one I know, Ranko or Dragan, then Milan Bosancic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think you meant the witness to go through one by one of each item. Can we see just 7 -- page 7 in both versions. Both here it ends with the number 169. The B/C/S version stops here, but the English version goes on to page [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Mr. Reid has advised me that the additional pages should have been removed when the document was uploaded, and they will be removed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. And then two further questions in relation to 65 ter number 23498 and 23499, while we grant the leave to add these documents to 65 ter list, but I note that two are identical documents while the latter is the one to which the witness added some additional marks. So I don't think we need to admit the first one. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I only have 65 ter number 23498.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are you not tendering 23499? It's on --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, you're right. No, but they were both -- yes, we only need one of them. You're right. I'm very sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No problem. And just to make sure the last -- the video-clips, 40573 A and B, although they are from the same video-clip, you are tendering those two separately.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's the way that -- --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- I was advised they should be tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Otherwise, are there any objections to the admission of associate exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. With the exception the 23498, all those will be admitted into evidence and be given numbers in due course by the court deputy. Well, Mr. Krejic, your testimony in other -- in the previous proceedings was admitted in it's entirety in lieu of your examination-in-chief in this trial. Now you will be further examined by Mr. Radovan Karadzic in his cross-examination. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Excellencies. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Krejic.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you for kindly meeting with the members of my Defence team. I hope that will help us conduct this cross-examination expeditiously, and I will try to put questions that could be answered with yes or no. I'm sorry that because of some administrative circumstances I was not able to meet with you personally. I just want you to know it did not depend on me. So that the Chamber and other participants in this process get an image of the area, I should like to ask you to mark certain points on a map, and I would like to call up 1D4275.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now zoom in on the beginning of the western third, where the cursor was. Exactly. Thank you. Could we now zoom in on Skender Vakuf. Now it's somewhere in the middle. Could we zoom in a bit more but still leave the neighbouring municipalities on the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krejic, may I ask for your assistance. This is an ethnic map of Knezevo which borders on Mrkonjic Grad, Banja Luka, Celinac, Kotor Varos, Jajce, and Travnik; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: I just don't understand if these are pre-war municipalities and the pre-war municipality of Knezevo or the current municipality of Knezevo after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm waiting for interpretation, and I would like you to do the same. This is a pre-war map, pre-war situation.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure it's pre-war. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll try to remind you. Is it true that the lower bottom concentration of 15, 20 villages in Okur [phoen], are these Croatian settlements across the Ugar canyon, which separates Croatian and Serbian settlements? I believe it's called Dobratic.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct. The entire area is called Pougarje, named after the Ugar River, and Dobratici was one of the four local communes before the war. And nowadays -- and this area was taken out of the pre-war Knezevo municipality to form a separate municipality called Dobratic which belongs to the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we agree to begin with that there are no Muslim villages in what remains and that the Muslims lived in Skender Vakuf, that is to say Knezevo?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes. We have just cleared that up with the Prosecutor. In the little town of Knezevo itself and two smaller suburbs, Sapani and Bastina, which are one kilometre from the centre of town each, they contained very few houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you mark Koricanske Stijene on this map very roughly, the place of the incident.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: I couldn't, because when I told you at the outset that I don't think it's a map of pre-war Knezevo, I believe it's a map of Knezevo as it is now, Koricani is now within the Knezevo municipality, whereas it was not before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you mark then the Ugar River and the concentration of Croatian places.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: The Ugar River, as you said, it's canyon separates -- I'm sorry about this. I don't know if I've drawn it correctly, but this red line separating the Croatian and Serbian population is where the Ugar River flows. My hand is shaking a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you mark Dobratic municipality with number 2.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And could you help us while the map is still on display, where Koricanske Stijene is, the site of the incident.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: I think that this boundary is the boundary separating the pre-war Knezevo from Travnik, and that's approximately where the river Ilomska runs, and that's where the site of the incident would be. Approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you put number 3 there.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And so that we make it easier for later, this Muslim concentration of villages, is it Siprage or Vecici?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: This is Siprage and the surrounding villages. Vecici is further to the north, next to Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mark Siprage with 4 and Vecici with 5.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And one more thing. Could you draw a line, to the best of your recollection, where the front line or the separation line was throughout the war. We lost some ground occasionally at Vlasici, but the remaining front line remained the same. Where was the front line in the summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes. You've corrected yourself in that last question. The front line did move throughout the war. And there was one front line up until the capture of Jajce, and after that it changed. Now you've said summer 1992. Do you want to know where the front line was then?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. The more important part is closer to Vlasici and Travnik, whereas Jajce was within our territory at some point, but I'm interested in the area closer to Travnik. Were these Travnik villages covered? Was the front line towards Vlasici within the boundaries of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Something like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Put number 6 there, please. That's the front line, the separation line at the time.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you did not fight with Dobratici all the time, did you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: I hope you don't mean myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Certainly not.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: No, especially at the beginning of the war there was an understanding between Knezevo municipality -- or, rather, that part of Knezevo municipality made up of Croats that we should avoid conflict of all sorts, and we had no reason to fight anyway. You've already mentioned that there's a deep canyon of the Ugar River there, and it has always separated the 100 per cent Croatian area on one side and the Serbian side. There was no reason for war between them, and we displayed restraint and containment until the war when some other circumstances that prevailed that were beyond the control of the civilian authorities of Knezevo or Dobratici. We had a sort of gentlemen's agreement until then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before we remove this map, could you please confirm that towards the south closer to Travnik and Jajce there was constant fighting, and at Vlasici the front line moved all the time depending on the successes achieved, and they were the successes of the other side rather than ours? Did it move all the time?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: I apologise. We advanced only in 1992 when Jajce fell, when we took Jajce and the Croatian part of Knezevo municipality, but we are talking about the slopes of Vlasici and Galica mountain in the direction of Turbe. Throughout the war, the line that I marked by number 6 was exactly as you defined it. We did not make any advancements. It was as it was. And then in the course of 1994, we suffered losses, which means that the line was moved, but it was moved at our expense.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now could you please tell us -- you mentioned in the case of Ivankovic in Sarajevo that the unit under the command of a serious man, Slobodan Celic, was the closest to the place of the event. However, according to you, that unit was a few kilometres away from the -- the event. It was closer to the front line; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please put number 7 next to the place where that unit, the closest unit, that is, was deployed.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I'm really not very good at making the markings. The markings should be a bit more to the right, on the very border. It would be more or less here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please put number 7 under your marking.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You seem to be right, because there is a border next to number 3. It is possible that the municipality border was there before the war. And now can you please put the date on the map, and can you sign it.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1880, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to immediately move on to the key tragic event in the Ivankovic case, which is 65 ter 22155. 65 ter 22155, on page 11, you stated that Mr. Zupljanin ordered you to take a professional from the police with you and to go to place of the event to see what had happened and then to urgently come back to Knezevo and report back to him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the same case, on page 13 you stated that the purpose of that was for you to provide your chief with the highest quality information. You were supposed to learn the details first, and then you were supposed to get in touch with the police unit, a platoon that was subordinated to the Army of the Republika Srpska and was deployed somewhere in the vicinity during the time when fighting was going on for Jajce; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then you were asked where that was, and you said that it was some 4 or 5 kilometres forward, and you have just marked the place where that unit was deployed at the separation line -- or, rather, the front line; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 14, in the same case you described your conversation with the commander Slobodan Celic, whom you highly respected, and you said that during that conversation, several people approached you. They all had impressions to share with you and about your encounter with the perpetrators, policemen from Prijedor, and you said that the policemen from Prijedor showed money, gold, and also that one of them allegedly said that he had secured the future of his whole family. Did they tell you that the other people did not hide anything and that they showed a lot of interest in the valuables that they had stolen from the victims?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: According to what police members from my public security station told me, one could say that that was indeed the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you gain an impression in all that that there was a rather small group of perpetrators and that a very important motive, if not the only one, was financial gain, the financial gain that was acquired in such a gruesome way? You're a policeman. When they told you how they had behaved, did you get an impression that that group was not big and that they were motivated by theft?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I immediately knew that the group was not big. However, I could also say that one of the motives was theft. I can agree with you on that. However, I thought then, and I still think now, that those men were just sick. They were mental cases, if I can put it that way, because only a lunatic, a sick mind, can commit such a crime. And then I would put theft and -- theft and financial gain in the second -- second place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the same case, on page 14 you explained that you had a telephone conversation with Mr. Zupljanin, that you conveyed information to him, and then he ordered you to come to the centre early in the morning, to the security services centre in Banja Luka, together with the president of the municipality and the president of the executive board, and you did that on the following morning, and that was your first meeting with Mr. Zupljanin after the event; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was my first and only meeting with Mr. Zupljanin, because Mr. Zupljanin did not attend the second meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then on page 15, you went on to say that Mr. Zupljanin called the meeting to order and that the meeting started by him saying that something terrible had happened, something that should not have happened. Were you then clear? Did you understand that Mr. Zupljanin was horrified by the event?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then on page 16 of the same transcript in the same case, you explained that people from Prijedor were also present there, and you repeated that -- or, rather, it was repeated in the summary. And you said in your testimony that you remember that he said to people from Prijedor that not a single murder can be covered up or may be covered up. Even if we all agree that we should cover up one single murder, it cannot be done. And there's no chance in hell that such a mass murder could be covered up, and we will certainly not do anything in that direction. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then in the Zecevic case, which is 1D4547 to the Prosecutor's question as to whether Mr. Zupljanin spoke about the perpetrators of the crime and the need for them to be arrested, you answered that Mr. Zupljanin took the position that everything had to be done by the book, according to the law, including an on-site investigation, the identification of the bodies and everything else that is envisaged by the law; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we then conclude that at that first meeting your assessment and your impression was that your chief, the chief of the security services centre, Mr. Zupljanin, acted in a very professional way as regards -- as regarded that crime?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the Zupljanin case, which is 1D4548 - now it has a 92 ter or P number - on page 14048 to the Prosecutor's question as to how Mr. Zupljanin reacted to all that, you said: "When I met Chief Zupljanin privately, that morning before the meeting I noticed that he was rather upset. He was visibly upset. He condemned the incident very clearly in no uncertain terms." I'm going to read in English. "[In English] He condemned the incident strenuously as he called a spade a spade. He said it was a crime, and he took more or less the same position as we from Knezevo did." [Interpretation] Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the same page, starting with line 11, you say that there was a lot of clamour. Zupljanin insisted that the bodies should be removed from the place of the incident, that the bodies should be identified and finally buried, and at one point he reacted very fiercely towards Simo Drljaca. "[In English] He told him in no uncertain terms that he would insist on Prosecuting the perpetrators of this -- of that crime." [Interpretation] Did you confirm in the Zupljanin case that Mr. Zupljanin lost his calm and started shouting when somebody mentioned a possibility of covering up the crime, that Zupljanin lost it at that point?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I knew Mr. Zupljanin. He was quite a composed person. I had never seen him react in that way, not before that or after that event. Not only did he shout, but he also threatened and waved his finger at people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You went on to say on page 14078 and 14079, and I will read in English. "[In English] Zupljanin was stunned and he said loud and clear, are you aware that one murder or crime cannot be concealed, let alone crime of this massive scale? Forget about it. We have to be serious and get our act together and deal with the -- in a proper way." [Interpretation] And then you went on to say on the following page. [In English] "This is a crime." [Interpretation] And then to the question: "[In English] And then you said earlier, he said at that point that there would be an investigation and the perpetrators would be punished." [Interpretation] Your answer: [In English] "Yes, because as I remember, Simo Drljaca again reacted with contempt towards what Stojan Zupljanin said. And I must say I had never seen Stojan Zupljanin lose his calm. This time he was really wagging his finger and saying that somebody --" [Interpretation] Very well. So you repeated this verbatim before the court of Bosnia-Herzegovina and in the case here at this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was indeed the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in the Zecevic case, which is 1D4547, on page 14 you stated that Zupljanin reiterated that that was a horrendous crime and that he was reading from a dispatch or a message where it said that the president of the Republika Srpska, Karadzic, who at the time was attending a peace conference either in London or somewhere else, had said that they had to deal with that, that their leaderships of the two municipalities had to deal with that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, you did not see whether it was a dispatch or a message noted down in some way. That was Stojan's interpretation.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: He was holding some sort of document that looked like the dispatches that we used to receive, normally, and I thought then and still think now that I couldn't be 100 per cent sure. It's possible it was a dispatch, because it was nothing difficult to type up on the communication device that we used at the time, the teletype, and it wasn't difficult to display it as if it had been sent to us from somewhere, but knowing Chief Zupljanin, I'm more inclined to think that he made up the whole story with the dispatch in order to drop your name to get more authority among the people of Prijedor on whom he otherwise had no great influence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It seems to follow from that that the residents of Prijedor were rather independent even from Banja Luka, which was no more than 50 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: I will limit my answer only to my line of work, that is to say public security. Indeed, when we had meetings before the war and during the war, Chief Zupljanin held these meetings at the collegium, attended by all chiefs of public security centres in the area of Banja Luka, and at these meetings we gained a very clear impression, in fact it was perfectly clear, that he had next to no influence at all on the leading people from the public security station of Prijedor, and I mean first and foremost Simo Drljaca. And even the other public security stations, Novi Grad, Bosanska Dubica, and other places at the foot of Mount Kozara acted similarly to Simo Drljaca, and I believe that was one of the reasons why the centre of public security of Prijedor was established as separate from Banja Luka; wherein, the Prijedor Public Security Station became the leader, whereas the other stations that I enumerated fell under that centre and thus definitively broke up with Banja Luka for which they had no great respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The others probably don't know this, but the Serbs have this autonomous streak. Whenever they can, they want to be independent from the superior level of management or whatever.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. That's one of our great flaws as a people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the Ivankovic case, 65 ter 22155, pages 18 and 19, you were asked about the survivors. Prosecutor Terzic asked you about the survivors, and then you explained that the people from the military security brought a man one morning, and the man was around 40, short, and he was turned over to you. They said they had found him wandering blindly in the area where the incident had happened. You informed Chief Zupljanin, and he told you that you should get in your car, go get the man, and that you were personally responsible for his health and safety and for bringing him to Banja Luka. Can you conclude from that that Zupljanin had a concern that somebody might wish to remove that witness, the eyewitness of the event, if they ever learned of his existence?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then you continued on page 19 of the same document talking to Prosecutor Terzic. You said you were sitting together in the car. You didn't notice that the man had any injuries, and he seemed comforted by your words that this deed had been perpetrated by people who were not really human and that it was a horrible crime, but he didn't say anything.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: I don't think you understood very well what I said, actually. Everything is true in your question except that he was comforted or acted positively. He didn't react in any way at the beginning, either positively or negatively. He seemed frozen, and he did not even seem to be a fully alive person who would dare to speak up or say anything. He didn't even seem like he was fully conscious. I was trying to comfort him, to say that what happened, happened, but now you are safe. What was done was obviously done by savages, beasts. But at first he didn't react in any way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, if it is convenient, we will take a break now. We will resume at 20 to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You -- you are right. I'm sorry. I'm trying not to read. I'm trying to interpret what it says so that we would gain time. So I'll try to be as specific as possible, that is. When you testified in Zupljanin, pages 14048, 1D4548 is the number -- or, rather, 92 ter, from line 21 onwards you were asked whether you talked to Zupljanin about what would happen to the survivor that you brought. So you said that you asked and that he said to you that this person would be handed over to the Swiss Red Cross. Was it clear to you that Zupljanin believed that it was better to hand him over to an International Red Cross than any local institution or the federation?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Transcript page again, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 14048.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is the page that we saw earlier on, but I don't find that passage on that page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From line 21 through 24. Maybe I have the wrong reference. Actually, we can look at the top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But as a matter of fact, if it is already in the transcript, you don't have to reconfirm it with the witness, because it is already in the evidence. Let's proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Then I'm not going to discuss at any length what you already said in your testimony that has been admitted as a whole. I'd like to ask about this second meeting. You discuss that in the Ivankovic et al case; that is, 65 ter number 22155, on pages 20 and 21. The Prosecutor, Ms. Terzic, asked you -- actually, you said that the task had not been accomplished and then you were asked to come back to this meeting that was attended by Branko Buhovac as a crime scene officer, and at that meeting what was discussed was whether an on-site investigation had been carried out at all, and you said, I'm going to read this out --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The speaker will have to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "[No interpretation]... no specific tasks. However, he was the most professional among us, and he said that before any relocation is carried out the person has to be identified. Quite literally all persons. And after that the persons should be buried." That question has to be resolved; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 21, the Prosecutor asked you whether Mr. Subotic, at the time minister of defence and colonel -- right? He was a colonel and minister of defence at the time, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: He was minister of defence. That's 100 per cent sure. But I think he was a general.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps he became a general later. So the prosecutor asked you -- Prosecutor Terzic asked you whether he had any proposals regarding the bodies, and you said that he chaired the meeting and that he seriously intended for that meeting to be fruitful to yield certain results, and to adopt conclusions that have to be carried out. Now, you say the people from Prijedor were a minority with regard to this particular position, to hide things as if nothing had happened. That was no longer the case?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At that point in time, did it become clear to you that they were afraid of being held potentially responsible for what their policemen had done and that they feared the reaction of the authorities, the top leadership of the republic as represented there by Subotic?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us see what you said about that on page 28 in the Ivankovic case. Bazdarevic Defence counsel, asked you to explain the behaviour of the late Drljaca and his behaviour at that other meeting where he was no longer in favour of that other option, and you said that you have a certain assumption that he was more peaceful at the other meeting because the meeting opened by General Subotic by starting to question Simo Drljaca as to who had issued orders to him to have the civilian population moved out of Prijedor. He started it like a serious investigation. You say that this was the second time in your life that you saw Simo Drljaca. You knew that he was always courageous, loud, a show-off, but all of a sudden he calmed down and he was answering the questions almost in a whisper; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Subotic himself spoke less about getting the bodies. He spoke more about the relocation of the population. That is on this same page 28.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Sorry, could you repeat that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Perhaps this is how I'm going to phrase it. Actually, I'll read it. You say that he spoke in a whisper and answered questions as if he were confused when he was answering General Subotic's questions. So maybe that was the reason. The way in which the meeting was opened resembled an investigation regarding the relocation of the population, then a meeting which was called in order to resolve the problem of how to get the bodies out. So your impression was that Subotic first wanted to see how come this population transfer occurred; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's not that that was my impression. That's the way it was. During the first part of this meeting, as I said in this transcript that you've been reading from, the meeting was devoted to these issues related to the transfer of the population, a serious investigation in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When Drljaca tried to say that someone from the authorities would have to know about that, Mr. Subotic was present, and he withdrew, and he could not prove that someone had known about that, but the regional level that was represented by Zupljanin and the republican level that was represented by Subotic unequivocally ruled out any possibility of hushing things up in any way. They said that everything had to be done in accordance with the law; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It's as if you had put two questions. Could you please separate the first part from the second part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You're right, and I'm in such a hurry. So as for the first questions put by Minister Subotic in terms of how come that happened, he tried to say that someone from the top leadership of the republic knew about that, but then he calmed down because he realized that Subotic was from the top leadership of the republic; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Perhaps you could put it that way. During my previous testimonies, I never said, because no one asked me, what the response was of Minister Subotic. Minister Subotic responded to Simo Drljaca that it was possible -- I mean, when Simo Drljaca said that the top leadership knew about that, Minister Subotic said that it is possible that orders -- some kind of orders or instructions came regarding the freedom of movement, primarily the non-Serb population in the territory of the municipality of Prijedor and throughout Republika Srpska; whereas, Simo and the other top people from Prijedor abused that. They understood it in their own way. And this population transfer that they carried out was in contravention of the efforts made by the leadership of the republic. That is what Minister Subotic said briefly, and then Simo Drljaca had no comment or answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the second part of the question. They calmed down, and they accepted that there had to be an investigation, as well as prosecution and trials, because Zupljanin and Subotic unequivocally said that they rule out any possibility of hushing things up; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Let me just say this once again. Zupljanin at the first meeting and Subotic at the second meeting, because the two of them did not attend meetings at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to show you some documents that have to do with the investigation, because that is your profession and you were in the area. 65 ter 18438. Can we have a look at that, please. Let us please have a look at the English version as well, because the telegram is barely legible in Serbian, but the English version will be all right. So I'd like to read it out to you in English. "[In English] Serbian Republic MUP dispatch number so-and-so 31st of August, 1992. Banja Luka security service centre, to the chief. "Order. "I hereby order you, in accordance with some regulations to conduct a full investigation regarding the deaths -- deaths of 150 Muslims in the territory of municipality Vakuf, Koricanske Stijene. "Inform this ministry of the results of the investigation, and in the event," something illegible, "the said allegations against the perpetrators, initiate legal accountability. "Minister, Mico Stanisic." [Interpretation] Have you heard or known that Stanisic had ordered an investigation as well down his own chain in the ministry?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: No. No. And the reason is the following: On the 1st of September, 1992, I was transferred to another job and left Knezevo, went to Banja Luka, and I see that that was written on the 31st of August. So, in fact, that was the day when I was no longer chief of the public security station of Knezevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you did know that an investigation continued; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: At my new job I didn't do anything that was related to this particular incident. However, as an inhabitant of Knezevo, because my wife and child had stayed on in Knezevo, so I came there and like anybody else who lived there I heard certain stories, certain details that may or may not be true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can it be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1881, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we take a look at 65 ter 12589. 12589.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm told that it hasn't been released yet.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we then have a look at 5780. That would be the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is the usual way in which things are done. Mr. Zupljanin as chief of centre in his telegram quotes the entire order of Minister Stanisic, and then he adds his own order related to this order. It says that you should take written statements about the events that took place from the policemen that escorted the convoy on the 21st of August and that they should be delivered personally. Is this the usual way things are done within an investigation?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's the standard way of communicating, and in some other situations Chief Zupljanin communicated with me in the same way. In a previous answer when I said I knew nothing about this, I meant that my line of work had nothing to do with it, but to be completely unequivocal, I believe these are authentic documents, and I have no reason to doubt that it all happened as described here. It's just that I had nothing to do with it in my work.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit D1882.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's Exhibit P3763, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now look at -- thank you. Could we look at 65 ter 20522. Was this already exhibited by the Prosecution? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In this document, Mr. Drljaca is replying to the chief of centre in Banja Luka regarding the dispatch he had received, and he said he's unable to conduct an investigation because those who were accompanied the convoy are currently on the front line in Han Pijesak. That's the eastern part of Republika Srpska; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's in the eastern part of Republika Srpska. What is your question about the dispatch of SJB Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I will. He's just saying here that he can't provide a list because the public security station did not organise the convoys. It only provided a certain number of policemen as guards at the request of the army and the Red Cross. Do you agree with this, or do you think that they were still afraid of Zupljanin and Subotic?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: In this first part of the dispatch, and this is only my opinion, of course, we see obvious obstruction on the part of Simo Drljaca. He's pretending these people are on a different planet and completely unavailable to be investigated. And in this second paragraph, it's obvious that he wants -- and again this is only my opinion because I don't know who organised the convoys. My job had nothing to do with this. But I did have occasion to get to know Simo Drljaca better in 1995 and 1996 when he worked in the centre in Banja Luka. This to me is vintage Simo Drljaca, his attempts to distance himself from the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1882, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In this Ivankovic case, 65 ter 22155, responding to a question by Madam Prosecutor, Mrs. Terzic, when she asked you about the position of Prijedor at this second meeting, you said they were cooperative about the proposal that things should be done properly, and the prosecutor asks whether you noticed this spirit of co-operation only at the second meeting that was chaired by General Subotic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You confirmed that at the next page, page 23, namely that the defence minister was very serious in leading the whole operation to make sure that things be done thoroughly and properly.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You've already mentioned this autonomy of the municipalities. Do you agree that more or less all the municipalities liked to behave as if they were a state within a state, not only Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes. You put it very well, a state within a state. And you can see the same thing today in peacetime.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the Stanisic case, on page 14067, I'll read your answer in English, line 15: "[In English] Some of the public security stations, and I mean in particular Prijedor and Simo Drljaca, were disobedient, to put it mildly. Undisciplined. They did what they wanted in performing their everyday law enforcement tasks." [Interpretation] It's consistent with your knowledge about our typical lack of discipline.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Earlier today I have said that Prijedor was amongst the worst in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Until they broke up with Banja Luka indefinitely and started acting independently.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes. When I say "Prijedor," I mean the public security station of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that during your tenure and even after you moved to Banja Luka you did not know the names of the perpetrators, and you spoke about that in the Ivankovic case 65 ter 22155 on page 27. You were asked: "While you occupied that post there and later in Banja Luka, did you ever find out the identities of the perpetrators?" And you answered: "No."

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Let me say this once again. The site of the crime did not fall under the purview of the public security station of Knezevo where I was chief. I was therefore in no way involved in the investigation, and even if the names of the perpetrators had been found, I would not have learnt about them. When I moved to Banja Luka, I became involved in totally different affairs and did not know anything about this. So with all due respect to the victims and the families of the victims and the survivors and everyone in any way connected with the Koricanske Stijene incident, I do not know to this day who these people were, regardless of the fact that I testified in the Ivankovic and Zecevic cases, and I wasn't interested, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it a good tradition in law enforcement agencies that people do not display any interest in things that are not directly part of their job?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: From my point of view, yes, it is, like in any other kind of work. My current job has to do with sapping and removing mines in Sarajevo, and I am not at all interested in the department that deals with IDs and passports, what numbers they're going to put on papers and what forms they're going to use. That is not my job, and that's the same attitude as I had earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see 65 ter 16231, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please look at this. Is this the security services centre? In fact, it is written to the security services centre by the public prosecutor's office. They say they received a criminal report, and now they request that the necessary information be collected on identify -- unidentified perpetrators. It says "NN perpetrators," which in our language means unidentified; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor has already gotten involved here but through the Ministry of the Interior, and he's giving instructions to the MUP as to what the police should do; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1883, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at 65 ter 18440.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the correspondence between the chief of centre in Banja Luka and the chief of the public security station in Prijedor. This is a request to provide a detailed written report on the incident at Koricanske Stijene near Knezevo, and the request specifies what information is needed, which policemen escorted the convoy, what their assignment was, to include all the active-duty and reserve policemen escorting the convoy. They ask if there was anyone else in the escort apart from policemen and what the policemen -- what the policemen wrote in their individual reports. Do you see that Mr. Zupljanin put four very serious tasks before the public security station in Prijedor? Do you believe that this is perfectly regular? He does not desist in his demands from Prijedor, and he insists that it's their obligation.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree it was completely regular. He is not giving up. And I see this last line where he says: "I hereby request again that you act on and reply to our dispatches ..." To me it sounds like a warning to the chief in Prijedor. He makes it plain that the chief in Prijedor had not fulfilled his previous task, and he requests an answer to this dispatch.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1884; Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at 65 ter 5783.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is Drljaca's reply to Chief Zupljanin. He says he has already provided an answer, and he refers to some people who are currently on the front line and have nothing to do with the incident at Koricanske Stijene. So something is being done but not much, really.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: As far as I can see, he's being evasive. Only in the first sentence does he mention the people who perpetrated the crime, and he confirms that they are near Han Pijesak, on the front line. The rest of the dispatch is about people who are not guilty, who had nothing to do with the convoy. So he's avoiding the demands made in the previous dispatches.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1885, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we briefly look at 1D4533, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Vlado Mandic, one of the deputies to the public prosecutor, is returning the documents accompanying the criminal report so that they could meet the demands made on 21 September 1999, to complete the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1886, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree -- or, rather, did you find out that those people were tried pursuant to the first batch of investigative documents dating back to 1992?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't understand your question. Could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You testified in at least two cases here, one was Ivankovic and the other was Zecevic. Do you agree -- or, rather, did you learn that the first or the initial results of investigation were grounds for criminal prosecution?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. I can't answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your position was that what had happened was a terrible crime, and you were particularly sensitive to the incident because it happened near Knezevo, although it was not in your municipality. That's why in the Stanisic case, on page 14046, you said, amongst other things, that -- I will read from line 8: "[In English] I shared with him everything, and I had learned in the field and I also told him what the position was taken by the key people in the Knezevo municipality, the people in the leadership." And then they asked you what position that was: "[In English] And in fact, the whole population, the members of the police force, of the army in the municipality of Knezevo condemned vigorously the attack, and they were appalled by what had happened, particularly because in our municipality there had been no war crimes nor mass or multiple murders and the public saw this indictment -- incident as something that is going to besmirch our municipality." [Interpretation] That was your position, and you also spoke about that -- or, rather, is this the case?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes, with the correction that we made at the beginning. I discussed that with the Prosecutor. I said that from this answer you may gain the impression that I believe that that was in our municipality, but it wasn't. It was not in Knezevo municipality. And as for your question, I can easily answer that with yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In Zecevic case -- on page 1 -- this is document 14547, page 15, you said that say you can say with certainty that nothing was ever taken over from any organ of the municipality of Knezevo that would facilitate the concealing of the bodies or any such thing. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: I said that not only did we not take over anything to facilitate the concealing of the body, but just the contrary was true. The leadership of the municipality and I as chief of the police station, as well as the general public in the municipality, was shocked, was appalled by that grave crime, and we were among those factors that put pressure on everybody to do things as quickly as possible and to remove the bodies as soon as possible and bury them in a dignified manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said in the Stanisic/Zupljanin case on page 14076 that it was a very inaccessible area and that it was very difficult to get to those bodies, that a whole set of equipment was necessary in order to access the site and the bodies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In that case, you were shown photos. I don't have the time to show them to you again. And in those photos, you marked the positions of the bodies; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now look at a photo, P3767. It wasn't shown, but it was admitted. And while we're waiting for it to appear on e-court, I'm going to remind you what you said on page 14100 in that case when you were asked to mark, you said: "Q. [In English] But it's very steep. Isn't it extreme? "A. Extremely. "Q. So we could say that these bodies below marked with the line and number 3 were 50 metres down roughly. Does that sound right? "A. From the road, yes." [Interpretation] Is this the site of the incident? Is this the slope which represented a problem when it came to removing the bodies, especially in view of the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes. The shape of the terrain was certainly one of the restricting factors when it came to taking the bodies out of the gorge. And another limiting factor was this road which is very narrow. It looks as if it was carved in the rock, which actually is the case. And this is the only road that connected the Vlasic plateau with Knezevo, and according to my free estimate, in that plateau there were about 10.000 people, including civilians and troops. I heard that when the -- the action was launched to remove the bodies that they had to interrupt their work very often to allow passage for the wounded, the army. So those were two restricting factors in the effort to remove the bodies from the gorge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you testified in the Ivankovic case, which is 22155 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just -- I was hesitant, but if you are really short of time for your cross-examination, the previous part, I can say, was unnecessary, because already they are in evidence, and you can rely on it at any time at a later stage for your submission, unless you are minded to supplement the witness's evidence in addition to what is already in our evidence. Please bear that in mind in the future, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellency. I simply wanted everybody to see how things looked like in this trial as well, but I will take your words into account.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's move on. Is it true that in the Stanisic proofing note, which is 1D4546, you confirm that the Skender Vakuf or Knezevo public security station did not have anything to do with the republican MUP in Pale after the 4th of -- the 4th of April, and that the communication lines were down up until the time when you left for Banja Luka on the 1st of September?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just explain the term "communications." That's direct communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As for Banja Luka, you could go there? You could establish telephone communication?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: We could go there, we could make telephone calls, or we could receive dispatches as well as the indirect dispatches from Sarajevo through Banja Luka and then to Knezevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are we talking about the year of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says here from the 4th or 5th April to the 1st September. I read that from the proofing note. The 1st September was the moment when he left to Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you probably don't know what happened later, whether Knezevo had communication lines, direct communication lines, with Pale. When you were in Knezevo that was not the case; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes, your interpretation is quite good.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Later on, on page 14028, in the Zupljanin/Stanisic case, you confirm that in 1992 you were not an SDS member. Although you were among its founders, you said that because of your profession you stopped being a party member of any party for that matter, not only of the SDS; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes. When I was selected as chief of the public security station in Knezevo, I stopped being an MP in the municipality of Knezevo, a member of the Municipal Board of SDS of Knezevo, and an MP in the Assembly of the autonomous province of Banja Luka. I froze my membership -- or, rather, I abandoned my membership in the SDS. I don't know if there were any other parties in existence at the time, and this is still my status.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 14097, you said that you had MPs from the SDA and the SDS that -- that you reached certain agreements before the conflict and that you had agreed -- or, rather, you favoured the option of Croats setting up their own municipality in their territory; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I said that at the beginning of this trial. We did not have any sticking points with the Croats, no arguments with the Croats. The leadership of the HDZ and the leadership of the SDS had very good relations, and there was also a good relationship between the leadership of the SDA and the SDS. For example, my school friend was the president of the SDA. Before the beginning of war, we had very good relations, and we co-operate -- co-operated very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that in our midst every newly set up municipality tries to speed up development and tries to improve the conditions of life? Wasn't that always a motive for all people to have their place proclaimed a municipality?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's absolutely correct. Let me just say in favour of that statement that the municipality of Knezevo was set up sometime in the 1960s, and there was a legal limit for a municipality to have a certain number of inhabitants. Since that condition was not met, the part with the Croatian population was taken from Jajce although it did not belong to Knezevo, and Croats actually did not benefit from that situation, and if they had become independent, I'm sure they would have moved forward much faster.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.
